citations.claim: just before violation speed is low, about to collide gap 0.005
after collision impulse speed spikes, causing controller force 486.9 > 72.67

counterfactual.change: Reduced intruding body 1 vx from 20.27 to 5 (single field change) to prevent high-energy collision impulse on controlled body; this keeps controller force within fmax and removes violation.

explanation: Controller uses kp*velocity-error law without clamping to fmax after impulse-driven velocity jump. At step 28 bodies 0 and 1 are touching (gap 0.005), collision impulse at the substep boundary spikes body 0's velocity from ~2.9 to 10.27 m/s at step 29. The resulting force command 486.9 greatly exceeds fmax 72.67. Reducing intruder velocity prevents the spike and the violation, confirming collision impulse is the cause and controller does not enforce fmax post-collision.
vision_note: From steps 26 to 27 the blue controller-driven body moves toward the green waypoint and closes on the small red body above it. At step 28 the two bodies are in contact, and at step 29 they have violently separated with the red body knocked outward, indicating a sudden collision impulse.
